sentences.zh: 皇帝寶璽皇后冊寶皇妃以下冊印皇太子冊寶皇太子妃冊寶親王以下冊寶冊印鐵券印信符節宮室制度臣庶室屋制度器用

translations.literal: Imperial seals; the empress's register and seal; registers and seals for imperial consorts of rank consort and below; the crown prince's register and seal; the crown princess's register and seal; registers and seals for princes of the blood of rank prince and below; iron tallies; official seals; tally plaques and tallies; palace regulations; regulations for commoners' dwellings and utensils
translations.idiomatic: Imperial seals; the empress's investiture register and seal; registers and seals for imperial consorts from Imperial Noble Consort downward; the crown prince's register and seal; the crown princess's register and seal; registers and seals for princes of the blood from full prince downward; iron tallies; official seals; tally plaques and tallies; regulations for palaces; regulations for commoners' houses and utensils

sentences.zh: 明初寶璽十七：其大者曰：「皇帝奉天之寶」，曰：「皇帝之寶」，曰：「皇帝行寶」，曰：「皇帝信寶」，曰：「天子之寶」，曰：「天子行寶」，曰：「天子信寶」，曰：「制誥之寶」，曰：「敕命之寶」，曰：「廣運之寶」，曰：「皇帝尊親之寶」，曰：「皇帝親親之寶」，曰：「敬天勤民之寶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Ming there were seventeen imperial seals: the larger ones were titled "Seal Received from Heaven by the Emperor," "Seal of the Emperor," "Traveling Seal of the Emperor," "Trust Seal of the Emperor," "Seal of the Son of Heaven," "Traveling Seal of the Son of Heaven," "Trust Seal of the Son of Heaven," "Seal for Proclamations and Edicts," "Seal for Commands," "Seal of Broad Fortune," "Seal of the Emperor Honoring Kin," "Seal of the Emperor Cherishing Kin," and "Seal of Revering Heaven and Diligently Serving the People."
translations.idiomatic: In early Ming there were seventeen imperial seals. The principal ones were titled "Seal Received from Heaven by the Emperor," "Seal of the Emperor," "Traveling Seal of the Emperor," "Trust Seal of the Emperor," "Seal of the Son of Heaven," "Traveling Seal of the Son of Heaven," "Trust Seal of the Son of Heaven," "Seal for Proclamations and Edicts," "Seal for Commands," "Seal of Broad Fortune," "Seal of the Emperor Honoring Kin," "Seal of the Emperor Cherishing Kin," and "Seal of Revering Heaven and Diligently Serving the People."

sentences.zh: 又有「御前之寶」、「表章經史之寶。

translations.literal: There were also the "Seal Before the Throne" and the "Seal for Memorials and Classics and Histories."
translations.idiomatic: There were also the "Seal Before the Throne" and the "Seal for Memorials and Classics and Histories."

sentences.zh: 」及「欽文之璽」。

translations.literal: " and the "Seal of Imperial Writings."
translations.idiomatic: It also included the "Seal of Imperial Writings."

sentences.zh: 丹符出驗四方。

translations.literal: Cinnabar tallies were issued to verify the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Cinnabar tallies were dispatched to verify credentials throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年欲制寶璽，有賈胡浮海獻美玉，曰：「此出于闐，祖父相傳，當為帝王寶璽。

translations.literal: In Hongwu 1 (1368), when the court wished to cast imperial seals, a merchant from abroad who had crossed the sea presented fine jade, saying, "This came from Khotan; my forefathers handed it down, and it ought to serve as the emperor's imperial seal."
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 1 (1368), as the court prepared to cast imperial seals, a foreign merchant who had come by sea presented a piece of fine jade, saying, "This stone came from Khotan and has been handed down in my family; it is fit to become the emperor's imperial seal."

sentences.zh: 」乃命制為寶，不知十七寶中，此玉製何寶也。

translations.literal: " The emperor then ordered it made into a seal, but it is not known which of the seventeen seals this jade became.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ordered it fashioned into a seal, but which of the seventeen seals was made from this jade is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 成祖又制「皇帝親親之寶」、「皇帝奉天之寶」、「誥命之寶」、「敕命之寶」。

translations.literal: The Chengzu Emperor also had cast the "Seal of the Emperor Cherishing Kin," the "Seal Received from Heaven by the Emperor," the "Seal for Proclamations," and the "Seal for Commands."
translations.idiomatic: The Chengzu Emperor also had cast the "Seal of the Emperor Cherishing Kin," the "Seal Received from Heaven by the Emperor," the "Seal for Proclamations," and the "Seal for Commands."

sentences.zh: 弘治十三年，鄠縣民毛志學於泥河濱得玉璽，其文曰：「受命於天，既壽永昌」。

translations.literal: In Hongzhi 13 (1500), Mao Zhixue, a commoner of Hu County, found a jade seal on the bank of the Ni River; its inscription read, "Having received the mandate from Heaven, long life and eternal prosperity."
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 13 (1500), a Hu County commoner named Mao Zhixue found a jade seal on the bank of the Ni River inscribed, "Having received the mandate from Heaven, long life and eternal prosperity."

sentences.zh: 色白微青，螭紐。

translations.literal: Its color was white with a slight greenish cast, and its knob was a hornless dragon.
translations.idiomatic: The stone was white with a faint bluish tint, and the knob was carved as a hornless dragon.

sentences.zh: 陝西巡撫熊翀以為秦璽復出，遣人獻之。

translations.literal: The Shaanxi grand coordinator Xiong Chong took it to be the Qin seal come forth again and sent men to present it.
translations.idiomatic: The Shaanxi grand coordinator Xiong Chong believed the Qin imperial seal had reappeared and dispatched envoys to present it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書傅瀚言：「自有秦璽以來，歷代得喪真偽之跡具載史籍。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Fu Han said, "Since the Qin seal first existed, the records in the histories of how each dynasty gained, lost, and judged the authenticity of seals are fully set down.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Fu Han said, "Since the time of the Qin seal, historical records have fully documented how each dynasty gained or lost it and how authenticity was judged.

sentences.zh: 今所進，篆文與《輟耕錄》等書摹載魚鳥篆文不同，其螭紐又與史傳所紀文盤五龍、螭缺一角、旁刻魏錄者不類。

translations.literal: The seal now presented differs from the fish-and-bird seal script copied in books such as the Record of Retiring to the Fields; its hornless-dragon knob also does not match what the histories describe—a patterned disk with five dragons, a hornless dragon missing one horn, and Wei inscriptions carved at the side.
translations.idiomatic: The seal now presented does not match the fish-and-bird seal script reproduced in works such as the Record of Retiring to the Fields, and its hornless-dragon knob does not accord with historical accounts of a patterned disk with five dragons, a hornless dragon missing one horn, and Wei-era inscriptions carved at the side.

sentences.zh: 蓋秦璽亡已久，今所進與宋、元所得，疑皆後世摹秦璽而刻之者。

translations.literal: The Qin seal has long been lost; what is now presented, like what the Song and Yuan obtained, is probably all work of later ages imitating the Qin seal in carving.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin seal has been lost for ages; what is now presented, like the seals obtained in Song and Yuan times, is probably a later imitation carved in the manner of the Qin seal.

sentences.zh: 竊惟璽之用，以識文書，防詐偽，非以為寶玩也。

translations.literal: I venture to consider that the use of seals is to authenticate documents and guard against fraud, not to treat them as precious curios.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view, seals exist to authenticate documents and prevent forgery, not to be treasured as curios.

sentences.zh: 自秦始皇得藍田玉以為璽，漢以後傳用之，自是巧爭力取，謂得此乃足以受命，而不知受命以德，不以璽也。

translations.literal: From the time Qin Shihuang obtained Lantian jade to make his seal and the Han thereafter transmitted its use, men have schemed and struggled to seize it, thinking that to obtain this object sufficed to receive the mandate—not knowing that the mandate is received through virtue, not through a seal.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since Qin Shihuang took Lantian jade for his seal and later dynasties passed it down, men have schemed and fought over it, believing possession of the stone alone conferred the mandate—forgetting that the mandate rests on virtue, not on a seal.

sentences.zh: 故求之不得，則偽造以欺人；

translations.literal: Thus when they could not obtain it, they forged one to deceive others;
translations.idiomatic: When they could not obtain the genuine seal, they forged one to deceive the world;

sentences.zh: 得之則君臣色喜，以誇示於天下。

translations.literal: when they obtained one, ruler and ministers rejoiced in countenance and displayed it to boast before all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: when they did obtain one, ruler and ministers rejoiced and paraded it before the realm.

sentences.zh: 是皆貽笑千載。

translations.literal: All such conduct has been a laughingstock for a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: All of this has been a laughingstock across the ages.

sentences.zh: 我高皇帝自製一代之璽，文各有義，隨事而施，真足以為一代受命之符，而垂法萬世，何藉此璽哉!。

translations.literal: Our August Founder fashioned seals for his own dynasty, each inscription with its own meaning, applied as the matter required—truly sufficient as the token of a dynasty's receiving the mandate and as a model for ten thousand generations. What need is there for this seal!
translations.idiomatic: Our August Founder fashioned seals for his own dynasty, each inscription bearing its own meaning and applied as occasion required—truly sufficient as the token of a dynasty's mandate and as a model for ten thousand generations. Why should we rely on this seal!

sentences.zh: 」帝從其言，卻而不用。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed his advice and returned the seal without using it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor accepted his advice and declined to use the seal.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十八年，新制七寶：曰：「奉天承運大明天子寶」、「大明受命之寶」、「巡狩天下之寶」、「垂訓之寶」、「命德之寶」、討罪安民之寶」、敕正萬民之寶」。

translations.literal: In Jiajing 18 (1539), seven new seals were cast: titled "Seal of the Great Ming Son of Heaven Who Receives the Mandate from Heaven and Carries Its Fortune," "Seal of the Great Ming Receiving the Mandate," "Seal for Touring the Realm," "Seal of Handing Down Instruction," "Seal of Mandating Virtue," "Seal for Punishing Crime and Pacifying the People," and "Seal for Correcting the Myriad People."
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 18 (1539), seven new seals were cast: the "Seal of the Great Ming Son of Heaven Who Receives the Mandate from Heaven and Carries Its Fortune," the "Seal of the Great Ming Receiving the Mandate," the "Seal for Touring the Realm," the "Seal of Handing Down Instruction," the "Seal of Mandating Virtue," the "Seal for Punishing Crime and Pacifying the People," and the "Seal for Correcting the Myriad People."

sentences.zh: 與國初寶璽共為禦寶二十四，尚寶司官掌之。

translations.literal: Together with the early Ming imperial seals they made twenty-four imperial seals in all, kept in charge by officials of the Imperial Seals Office.
translations.idiomatic: Together with the early Ming seals, there were twenty-four imperial seals in all, entrusted to the officials of the Imperial Seals Office.

sentences.zh: 皇后之冊：用金冊二片，依周尺長一尺二寸，廣五寸，厚二分五釐。

translations.literal: The empress's register: two gold leaves were used, by Zhou measure one foot two inches long, five inches wide, and two and a half fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: For the empress's investiture register, two gold leaves were used, measuring by the Zhou foot one foot two inches long, five inches wide, and two and a half fen thick.

sentences.zh: 字依數分行，鐫以真書。

translations.literal: Characters were divided into lines according to their number and engraved in regular script.
translations.idiomatic: The text was divided into lines according to character count and engraved in regular script.

sentences.zh: 上下有孔，聯以紅絛，開闔如書帙，藉以紅錦褥。

translations.literal: Holes were bored top and bottom and joined with red cord; they opened and closed like a book case and rested on a red brocade mat.
translations.idiomatic: Holes at top and bottom were joined with red cord so the leaves opened and closed like a book case, resting on a red brocade mat.

sentences.zh: 冊盝用木，飾以渾金瀝粉蟠龍，紅紵絲襯裏，內以紅羅銷金小袱裹冊，外以紅羅銷金夾袱包之，五色小絛縈於外。

translations.literal: The register case was of wood, ornamented with coiled dragons in full gold powder, lined with red pongee silk; within, a small gold-brocaded red gauze wrapper enclosed the register, and without, a gold-brocaded red gauze double wrapper bound it, with small cords of five colors wound around the outside.
translations.idiomatic: The register case was wooden, ornamented with coiled dragons in full gold powder and lined with red pongee silk; inside, a small gold-brocaded red gauze wrapper held the register, and outside, a gold-brocaded red gauze double wrapper bound it, wound about with small cords of five colors.

sentences.zh: 寶用金，龜紐，篆文曰：「皇后之寶」，依周尺方五寸九分，厚一寸七分。

translations.literal: The seal was of gold, with a tortoise knob; the seal script read "Seal of the Empress," and by Zhou measure it was five inches nine fen square and one inch seven fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: The seal was of gold with a tortoise knob, inscribed in seal script "Seal of the Empress," and by the Zhou foot measured five inches nine fen square and one inch seven fen thick.

sentences.zh: 寶池用金，闊取容。

translations.literal: The seal tray was of gold, broad enough to receive the seal.
translations.idiomatic: The seal tray was of gold, sized to receive the seal.

sentences.zh: 寶篋二副，一置寶，一置寶池。

translations.literal: There were two sets of seal caskets, one holding the seal and one the seal tray.
translations.idiomatic: There were two sets of seal caskets, one for the seal and one for the seal tray.

sentences.zh: 每副三重：外篋用木，飾以渾金瀝粉蟠龍，紅紵絲襯裏；

translations.literal: Each set had three layers: the outer casket was of wood, ornamented with coiled dragons in full gold powder and lined with red pongee silk;
translations.idiomatic: Each set had three layers: the outer casket was wooden, ornamented with coiled dragons in full gold powder and lined with red pongee silk;

sentences.zh: 中篋用金鈒蟠龍；

translations.literal: the middle casket was of gold-inlaid coiled dragons;
translations.idiomatic: the middle casket was of gold-inlaid coiled dragons;

sentences.zh: 內小篋飾如外篋，內置寶座，四角雕蟠龍，飾以渾金。

translations.literal: the inner small casket was ornamented like the outer; within was set a seal stand, with coiled dragons carved at the four corners and ornamented in full gold.
translations.idiomatic: the inner small casket matched the outer in ornament; inside stood a seal pedestal with coiled dragons carved at the four corners and finished in full gold.

sentences.zh: 座上用錦褥，以銷金紅羅小夾袱裹寶，其篋外各用紅羅銷金大夾袱覆之。

translations.literal: On the stand was a brocade mat; the seal was wrapped in a small gold-brocaded red gauze double wrapper, and outside each casket a large gold-brocaded red gauze double wrapper covered it.
translations.idiomatic: A brocade mat lay on the stand; the seal was wrapped in a small gold-brocaded red gauze double wrapper, and each casket was covered outside with a large gold-brocaded red gauze double wrapper.

sentences.zh: 臨冊之日，冊寶俱置於紅髹輿案，案頂有紅羅瀝水，用擔牀舉之。

translations.literal: On the day of investiture, register and seal were both placed on a red-lacquered carrying table; the top of the table had a red gauze valance, and it was borne on a carrying bed.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of investiture, register and seal were placed together on a red-lacquered carrying table with a red gauze valance at the top, borne on a carrying bed.

sentences.zh: 皇貴妃而下，有冊無寶而有印。

translations.literal: For imperial noble consorts and below, there was a register but no seal, only a stamp.
translations.idiomatic: From Imperial Noble Consort downward, investiture included a register but no seal, only an official stamp.

sentences.zh: 妃冊，用鍍金銀冊二片，廣長與後冊同。

translations.literal: For a consort's register, two gilt-silver leaves were used, of the same length and width as the empress's register.
translations.idiomatic: A consort's register used two gilt-silver leaves of the same dimensions as the empress's register.

sentences.zh: 冊盝飾以渾金瀝粉蟠鳳。

translations.literal: The register case was ornamented with coiled phoenixes in full gold powder.
translations.idiomatic: The register case was ornamented with coiled phoenixes in full gold powder.

sentences.zh: 其印用金，龜紐，尺寸與諸王寶同，文曰：「皇妃之印」。

translations.literal: The stamp was of gold, with a tortoise knob; its dimensions were the same as princes' seals, and the inscription read "Stamp of the Imperial Consort."
translations.idiomatic: The stamp was of gold with a tortoise knob, the same size as a prince's seal, inscribed "Stamp of the Imperial Consort."

sentences.zh: 篋飾以蟠鳳。

translations.literal: The casket was ornamented with coiled phoenixes.
translations.idiomatic: The casket was ornamented with coiled phoenixes.

sentences.zh: 宣德元年，帝以貴妃孫氏有容德，特請於皇太后，制金寶賜之，未幾即誕皇嗣。

translations.literal: In Xuande 1 (1426), because Imperial Consort Sun possessed grace and virtue, the emperor specially requested of the empress dowager that a gold seal be made and bestowed on her; before long she bore the imperial heir.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 1 (1426), finding Imperial Consort Sun possessed both grace and virtue, the emperor specially petitioned the empress dowager to have a gold seal cast and bestowed on her; before long she bore the imperial heir.

sentences.zh: 自是貴妃授寶，遂為故事。

translations.literal: From this time the bestowal of a seal on an imperial consort became precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the bestowal of a seal upon an imperial consort became established precedent.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十年，立九嬪，冊用銀，殺皇妃五分之一，以金飾之。

translations.literal: In Jiajing 10 (1531), when the nine secondary consorts were established, silver registers were used, reduced one-fifth from the imperial consort's measure and ornamented with gold.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 10 (1531), when the nine secondary consort ranks were established, silver registers were used, one-fifth smaller than the imperial consort's and ornamented with gold.

sentences.zh: 皇太子冊寶：冊用金，二片，其制及盝篋之飾與皇后冊同。

translations.literal: Crown prince's register and seal: the register used two gold leaves; its form and the ornament of case and casket were the same as the empress's register.
translations.idiomatic: For the crown prince's register and seal, two gold leaves formed the register; its form and the ornament of case and casket matched the empress's register.

sentences.zh: 寶用金，龜紐，篆書「皇太子寶」。

translations.literal: The seal was of gold, with a tortoise knob, and in seal script read "Seal of the Crown Prince."
translations.idiomatic: The seal was of gold with a tortoise knob, inscribed in seal script "Seal of the Crown Prince."

sentences.zh: 其制及池篋之飾與後寶同。

translations.literal: Its form and the ornament of tray and casket were the same as the empress's seal.
translations.idiomatic: Its form and the ornament of tray and casket matched the empress's seal.

sentences.zh: 皇太子妃冊寶：其冊用金，兩葉，重百兩，每葉高一尺二寸，廣五寸。

translations.literal: Crown princess's register and seal: the register used gold, two leaves weighing one hundred taels; each leaf was one foot two inches high and five inches wide.
translations.idiomatic: For the crown princess's register and seal, the register was of gold in two leaves weighing one hundred taels; each leaf measured one foot two inches high and five inches wide.

sentences.zh: 藉冊以錦，聯冊以紅絲絛，墊冊以錦褥，裹冊以紅羅銷金袱。

translations.literal: The register rested on brocade, was joined with red silk cord, padded with a brocade mat, and wrapped in a gold-brocaded red gauze wrapper.
translations.idiomatic: The register rested on brocade, was bound with red silk cord, padded with a brocade mat, and wrapped in a gold-brocaded red gauze wrapper.

sentences.zh: 其盝飾以渾金瀝粉雲鳳，內有花銀釘鉸，嵌金絲鐵筦龠；

translations.literal: Its case was ornamented with cloud-and-phoenix designs in full gold powder; within were floral silver hinges, with gold-wire-inlaid iron pipes and locks;
translations.idiomatic: Its case was ornamented with cloud-and-phoenix designs in full gold powder; inside were floral silver hinges and gold-wire-inlaid iron locks;

sentences.zh: 外以紅羅銷金袱覆之。

translations.literal: without, a gold-brocaded red gauze wrapper covered it.
translations.idiomatic: outside, a gold-brocaded red gauze wrapper covered it.

sentences.zh: 其金寶之制未詳。

translations.literal: The specifications for its gold seal are not recorded in detail.
translations.idiomatic: The specifications of its gold seal are not recorded in detail.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十八年更定，止授金冊，不用寶。

translations.literal: In Hongwu 28 (1395) it was revised: only a gold register was conferred, and no seal was used.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 28 (1395) the regulations were revised so that only a gold register was conferred and no seal was used.

sentences.zh: 親王冊寶：冊制與皇太子同。

translations.literal: Princes of the blood, register and seal: the register followed the same form as the crown prince's.
translations.idiomatic: For princes of the blood, the register followed the crown prince's form.

sentences.zh: 其寶用金，龜紐，依周尺方五寸二分，厚一寸五分，文曰：「某王之寶」。

translations.literal: The seal was of gold, with a tortoise knob; by Zhou measure it was five inches two fen square and one inch five fen thick, and the inscription read "Seal of the Prince of Such-and-Such."
translations.idiomatic: The seal was of gold with a tortoise knob, five inches two fen square and one inch five fen thick by the Zhou foot, inscribed "Seal of the Prince of [name]."

sentences.zh: 池篋之飾，與皇太子寶同。

translations.literal: The ornament of tray and casket was the same as the crown prince's seal.
translations.idiomatic: The tray and casket matched those of the crown prince's seal.

sentences.zh: 寶盝之飾，則雕蟠螭。

translations.literal: The seal case, however, was carved with coiled hornless dragons.
translations.idiomatic: The seal case, however, was carved with coiled hornless dragons.

sentences.zh: 親王妃冊印：其金冊，高視太子妃冊減一寸，餘制悉同，冊文視親王。

translations.literal: Prince's consort, register and stamp: her gold register was one inch shorter in height than the crown princess's register; all other specifications were the same, and the text of the register followed that for a prince.
translations.idiomatic: For a prince's consort, the gold register was one inch shorter than the crown princess's register; all other specifications were the same, and the text followed that used for a prince.

sentences.zh: 其金印之制未詳。

translations.literal: The specifications for her gold stamp are not recorded in detail.
translations.idiomatic: The specifications of her gold stamp are not recorded in detail.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十八年更定，止授金冊。

translations.literal: In Hongwu 28 it was revised: only a gold register was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 28 (1395) the regulations were revised so that only a gold register was conferred.

sentences.zh: 公主冊印：銀冊二片，鐫字鍍金，藉以紅錦褥。

translations.literal: Imperial princess, register and stamp: two silver leaves, characters engraved and gilt, resting on a red brocade mat.
translations.idiomatic: For an imperial princess, two silver register leaves were used, the characters engraved and gilt, resting on a red brocade mat.

sentences.zh: 冊盝飾以渾金瀝粉蟠螭。

translations.literal: The register case was ornamented with coiled hornless dragons in full gold powder.
translations.idiomatic: The register case was ornamented with coiled hornless dragons in full gold powder.

sentences.zh: 其印同宋制，用金，龜紐，文曰：「某國公主之印」。

translations.literal: Her stamp followed Song practice: of gold, with a tortoise knob, the inscription reading "Stamp of the Princess of Such-and-Such State."
translations.idiomatic: Her stamp followed Song practice: of gold with a tortoise knob, inscribed "Stamp of the Princess of [state name]."

sentences.zh: 方五寸二分，厚一寸五分。

translations.literal: It was five inches two fen square and one inch five fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: It measured five inches two fen square and one inch five fen thick.

sentences.zh: 印池用金，廣取容。

translations.literal: The stamp tray was of gold, broad enough to receive it.
translations.idiomatic: The stamp tray was of gold, sized to receive the stamp.

sentences.zh: 印外篋用木，飾以渾金瀝粉盤鳳，中篋用金鈒蟠鳳，內小篋，飾如外篋。

translations.literal: The outer stamp casket was of wood, ornamented with coiled phoenixes in full gold powder; the middle casket was of gold-inlaid coiled phoenixes; the inner small casket was ornamented like the outer.
translations.idiomatic: The outer stamp casket was wooden, ornamented with coiled phoenixes in full gold powder; the middle casket was of gold-inlaid coiled phoenixes; the inner small casket matched the outer in ornament.

sentences.zh: 親王世子金冊金寶：承襲止授金冊，傳用金寶。

translations.literal: Heir apparent of a prince of the blood, gold register and gold seal: on succession only a gold register was conferred; the gold seal was transmitted for use.
translations.idiomatic: For the heir apparent of a prince of the blood, on succession only a gold register was conferred while the gold seal was transmitted for continued use.

sentences.zh: 世子妃亦用金冊。

translations.literal: The heir apparent's consort also received a gold register.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent's consort likewise received a gold register.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十三年鑄世子妃印，制視王妃，金印，龜紐，篆文曰：「某世子妃印」。

translations.literal: In Hongwu 23 (1390) the stamp for an heir apparent's consort was cast; its form followed the prince's consort's, a gold stamp with tortoise knob, seal script reading "Stamp of the Consort of the Heir Apparent of Such-and-Such."
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 23 (1390) a stamp for the heir apparent's consort was cast to the same specifications as a prince's consort's: a gold stamp with tortoise knob, inscribed in seal script "Stamp of the Consort of the Heir Apparent of [name]."

sentences.zh: 郡王，鍍金銀冊、鍍金銀印，冊文視世子。

translations.literal: For commandery princes, gilt-silver registers and gilt-silver stamps were used; the text of the register followed that for an heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Commandery princes received gilt-silver registers and gilt-silver stamps; the register text followed that used for an heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 其妃止有鍍金銀冊。

translations.literal: Their consorts received only gilt-silver registers.
translations.idiomatic: Their consorts received only gilt-silver registers.

sentences.zh: 功臣鐵券：洪武二年，太祖欲封功臣，議為鐵券，而未有定制。

translations.literal: Iron tallies for meritorious officials: In Hongwu 2 (1369), when the Taizu Emperor wished to enfeoff meritorious officials, iron tallies were discussed, but no fixed regulations yet existed.
translations.idiomatic: Iron tallies for meritorious officials: In Hongwu 2 (1369), as the Taizu Emperor prepared to enfeoff his meritorious followers, iron tallies were proposed, but no fixed regulations yet existed.

sentences.zh: 或言台州民錢允一有家藏吳越王鏐唐賜鐵券，遂遣使取之，因其式而損益焉。

translations.literal: Someone reported that Qian Yunyi, a commoner of Taizhou, had in his family a hoarded iron tally bestowed by the Tang on King Qian Liu of Wuyue; envoys were sent to fetch it, and the form was adjusted and reduced accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: It was reported that a Taizhou commoner named Qian Yunyi possessed in his family an iron tally the Tang had bestowed on King Qian Liu of Wuyue; envoys were dispatched to fetch it, and the court adapted its form with modifications.

sentences.zh: 其制如瓦，第為七等。

translations.literal: The form was like a roof tile, divided into seven grades.
translations.idiomatic: The tally was shaped like a roof tile and divided into seven grades.

sentences.zh: 公二等：一高尺，廣一尺六寸五分；

translations.literal: For dukes, two grades: one one foot high and one foot six inches five fen wide;
translations.idiomatic: For dukes there were two grades: one one foot high and one foot six inches five fen wide;

sentences.zh: 一高九寸五分，廣一尺六寸。

translations.literal: one nine inches five fen high and one foot six inches wide.
translations.idiomatic: one nine inches five fen high and one foot six inches wide.

sentences.zh: 侯三等：一高九寸，廣一尺五寸五分；

translations.literal: For marquises, three grades: one nine inches high and one foot five inches five fen wide;
translations.idiomatic: For marquises there were three grades: one nine inches high and one foot five inches five fen wide;

sentences.zh: 一高八寸五分，廣一尺五寸；

translations.literal: one eight inches five fen high and one foot five inches wide;
translations.idiomatic: one eight inches five fen high and one foot five inches wide;

sentences.zh: 一高八寸，廣一尺四寸五分。

translations.literal: one eight inches high and one foot four inches five fen wide.
translations.idiomatic: one eight inches high and one foot four inches five fen wide.

sentences.zh: 伯二等：一高七寸五分，廣一尺三寸五分；

translations.literal: For earls, two grades: one seven inches five fen high and one foot three inches five fen wide;
translations.idiomatic: For earls there were two grades: one seven inches five fen high and one foot three inches five fen wide;

sentences.zh: 一高六寸五分，廣一尺二寸五分。

translations.literal: one six inches five fen high and one foot two inches five fen wide.
translations.idiomatic: one six inches five fen high and one foot two inches five fen wide.

sentences.zh: 外刻履歷、恩數之詳，以記其功；

translations.literal: Without were engraved the details of career and grants of favor, to record their merit;
translations.idiomatic: The outer face recorded their careers and the details of favors granted, commemorating their merit;

sentences.zh: 中鐫免罪、減祿之數，以防其過。

translations.literal: within were cut the numbers of pardons and reductions in stipend, to guard against their faults.
translations.idiomatic: the inner face inscribed the number of pardons and stipend reductions allowed, to guard against future faults.

sentences.zh: 字嵌以金。

translations.literal: The characters were inlaid with gold.
translations.idiomatic: The characters were inlaid with gold.

sentences.zh: 凡九十七副，各分左右，左頒功臣，右藏內府，有故則合之，以取信焉。

translations.literal: In all there were ninety-seven pairs; each was divided into left and right—the left was bestowed on the meritorious official, the right stored in the inner palace; when occasion arose they were joined to verify authenticity.
translations.idiomatic: Ninety-seven pairs were made in all, each divided into left and right halves: the left was bestowed on the meritorious official, the right stored in the inner palace; when needed the halves were joined to verify authenticity.

sentences.zh: 三年，大封功臣，公六人，侯二十八人，並賜鐵券。

translations.literal: In the third year, meritorious officials were enfeoffed on a grand scale—six dukes and twenty-eight marquises—and all were granted iron tallies.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (1370) a great enfeoffment of meritorious officials was carried out—six dukes and twenty-eight marquises—and iron tallies were bestowed on all.

sentences.zh: 公：李善長、徐達、李文忠、馮勝、鄧愈、常茂。

translations.literal: Dukes: Li Shanchang, Xu Da, Li Wenzhong, Feng Sheng, Deng Yu, and Chang Mao.
translations.idiomatic: The dukes were Li Shanchang, Xu Da, Li Wenzhong, Feng Sheng, Deng Yu, and Chang Mao.

sentences.zh: 侯：湯和、唐勝宗、陸仲亨、周德興、華雲龍、顧時、耿炳文、陳德、郭子興、王志、鄭遇春、費聚、吳良、吳楨、趙庸、廖永忠、俞通源、華高、楊璟、康鐸、硃亮祖、傅友德、胡美、韓政、黃彬、曹良臣、梅思祖、陸聚。

translations.literal: Marquises: Tang He, Tang Shengzong, Lu Zhongheng, Zhou Dexing, Hua Yunlong, Gu Shi, Geng Bingwen, Chen De, Guo Zixing, Wang Zhi, Zheng Yuchun, Fei Ju, Wu Liang, Wu Zhen, Zhao Yong, Liao Yongzhong, Yu Tongyuan, Hua Gao, Yang Jing, Kang Duo, Zhu Liangzu, Fu Youde, Hu Mei, Han Zheng, Huang Bin, Cao Liangchen, Mei Sizu, and Lu Ju.
translations.idiomatic: The marquises were Tang He, Tang Shengzong, Lu Zhongheng, Zhou Dexing, Hua Yunlong, Gu Shi, Geng Bingwen, Chen De, Guo Zixing, Wang Zhi, Zheng Yuchun, Fei Ju, Wu Liang, Wu Zhen, Zhao Yong, Liao Yongzhong, Yu Tongyuan, Hua Gao, Yang Jing, Kang Duo, Zhu Liangzu, Fu Youde, Hu Mei, Han Zheng, Huang Bin, Cao Liangchen, Mei Sizu, and Lu Ju.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，改制鐵券，賜公傅友德，侯王弼、耿炳文、郭英及故公徐達、李文忠，侯吳傑、沐英，凡八家。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, iron tallies were reformed and bestowed on the duke Fu Youde, the marquises Wang Bi, Geng Bingwen, and Guo Ying, and posthumously on the former dukes Xu Da and Li Wenzhong and the marquises Wu Jie and Mu Ying—eight households in all.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year (1392) the iron tally was redesigned and granted to Duke Fu Youde, Marquises Wang Bi, Geng Bingwen, and Guo Ying, and posthumously to the former dukes Xu Da and Li Wenzhong and Marquises Wu Jie and Mu Ying—eight households in all.

sentences.zh: 永樂初，靖難功臣亦有賜者。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yongle reign, meritorious officials of the Pacification of Difficulties also received grants.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongle reign, meritorious officials of the Pacification of Difficulties also received iron tallies.

sentences.zh: 百官印信：洪武初，鑄印局鑄中外諸司印信。

translations.literal: Official seals for the hundred offices: At the beginning of Hongwu, the Seal-Casting Bureau cast seals for all offices within and without the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Official seals for the hundred offices: Early in Hongwu, the Seal-Casting Bureau cast seals for all offices inside and outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 正一品，銀印，三臺，方三寸四分，厚一寸。

translations.literal: Rank 1a: silver seal, three tiers, three inches four fen square, one inch thick.
translations.idiomatic: Rank 1a officials received a silver seal of three tiers, three inches four fen square and one inch thick.

sentences.zh: 六部、都察院並在外各都司，俱正二品，銀印二臺，方三寸二分，厚八分。

translations.literal: The Six Ministries, the Censorate, and all regional command commissions in the provinces were all rank 2a, with silver seals of two tiers, three inches two fen square and eight fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: The Six Ministries, the Censorate, and all regional command commissions in the provinces were rank 2a, with silver seals of two tiers, three inches two fen square and eight fen thick.

sentences.zh: 其餘正二品、從二品官，銀印二臺，方三寸一分，厚七分。

translations.literal: All other rank 2a and 2b officials had silver seals of two tiers, three inches one fen square and seven fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: All other rank 2a and 2b officials received silver seals of two tiers, three inches one fen square and seven fen thick.

sentences.zh: 惟衍聖公以正二品，三臺銀印，則景泰三年賜也。

translations.literal: Only the Duke of Yansheng, though rank 2a, received a silver seal of three tiers—granted in Jingtai 3 (1452).
translations.idiomatic: Only the Duke of Yansheng, though holding rank 2a, received a silver seal of three tiers—granted in Jingtai 3 (1452).

sentences.zh: 順天、應天二府俱正三品，銀印，方二寸九分，厚六分五釐。

translations.literal: The Shuntian and Yingtian prefectures were both rank 3a, with silver seals two inches nine fen square and six fen five li thick.
translations.idiomatic: The Shuntian and Yingtian prefectures were both rank 3a, with silver seals two inches nine fen square and six fen five li thick.

sentences.zh: 其餘正三品、從三品官，俱銅印，方二寸七分，厚六分。

translations.literal: All other rank 3a and 3b officials had bronze seals, two inches seven fen square and six fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: All other rank 3a and 3b officials received bronze seals two inches seven fen square and six fen thick.

sentences.zh: 惟太僕、光祿寺並在外鹽運司，俱從三品，銅印，方減一分，厚減五釐。

translations.literal: Only the Court of the Imperial Stud, the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and the salt transport commissions in the provinces, all rank 3b, had bronze seals one fen smaller in width and five li thinner.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Court of the Imperial Stud, the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and the provincial salt transport commissions, all rank 3b, received bronze seals one fen smaller in width and five li thinner.

sentences.zh: 正四品、從四品，俱銅印，方二寸五分，厚五分。

translations.literal: Rank 4a and 4b officials all had bronze seals, two inches five fen square and five fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: Rank 4a and 4b officials all received bronze seals two inches five fen square and five fen thick.

sentences.zh: 正五品、從五品，俱銅印，方二寸四分，厚四分五釐。

translations.literal: Rank 5a and 5b officials all had bronze seals, two inches four fen square and four fen five li thick.
translations.idiomatic: Rank 5a and 5b officials all received bronze seals two inches four fen square and four fen five li thick.

sentences.zh: 惟在外各州從五品，銅印，方減一分，厚減五釐。

translations.literal: Only rank 5b officials in the various prefectures in the provinces had bronze seals one fen smaller in width and five li thinner.
translations.idiomatic: Only rank 5b officials in provincial prefectures received bronze seals one fen smaller in width and five li thinner.

sentences.zh: 正六品、從六品，俱銅印，方二寸二分，厚三分五釐。

translations.literal: Rank 6a and 6b officials all had bronze seals, two inches two fen square and three fen five li thick.
translations.idiomatic: Rank 6a and 6b officials all received bronze seals two inches two fen square and three fen five li thick.

sentences.zh: 正七品、從七品，銅印，方二寸一分，厚三分。

translations.literal: Rank 7a and 7b officials had bronze seals, two inches one fen square and three fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: Rank 7a and 7b officials received bronze seals two inches one fen square and three fen thick.

sentences.zh: 正從八品，俱銅印，方二寸，厚二分五釐。

translations.literal: Rank 8a and 8b officials all had bronze seals, two inches square and two fen five li thick.
translations.idiomatic: Rank 8a and 8b officials all received bronze seals two inches square and two fen five li thick.

sentences.zh: 正從九品，俱銅印，方一寸九分，厚二分二釐。

translations.literal: Rank 9a and 9b officials all had bronze seals, one inch nine fen square and two fen two li thick.
translations.idiomatic: Rank 9a and 9b officials all received bronze seals one inch nine fen square and two fen two li thick.

sentences.zh: 未入流者，銅條記，闊一寸三分，長二寸五分，厚二分一釐。

translations.literal: Those outside the regular ranks had bronze strip seals, one inch three fen wide, two inches five fen long, and two fen one li thick.
translations.idiomatic: Officials outside the regular ranks received bronze strip seals one inch three fen wide, two inches five fen long, and two fen one li thick.

sentences.zh: 以上俱直紐，九疊篆文。

translations.literal: All the above had straight knobs and nine-fold seal script.
translations.idiomatic: All of the above had straight knobs and nine-fold seal script.

sentences.zh: 初，雜職亦方印，至洪武十三年始改條記。

translations.literal: At first miscellaneous offices also had square seals; only in Hongwu 13 (1380) were strip seals adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Initially miscellaneous offices also used square seals; strip seals were adopted only in Hongwu 13 (1380).

sentences.zh: 凡百官之印，惟文淵閣銀印，直紐，方一寸七分，厚六分，玉箸篆文，誠重之也。

translations.literal: Among all the hundred offices' seals, only the Hall of Literary Profundity had a silver seal, with straight knob, one inch seven fen square and six fen thick, in jade-brush seal script—a mark of genuine esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Among all official seals, only the Hall of Literary Profundity received a silver seal with a straight knob, one inch seven fen square and six fen thick, in jade-brush seal script—a mark of special esteem.

sentences.zh: 武臣受重寄者，徵西、鎮朔、平蠻諸將軍，銀印，虎紐，方三寸三分，厚九分，柳葉篆文。

translations.literal: Military officials entrusted with weighty commissions—the Pacify-the-West, Pacify-the-North, and Pacify-the-Barbarians generals—had silver seals with tiger knobs, three inches three fen square and nine fen thick, in willow-leaf seal script.
translations.idiomatic: Military officials entrusted with weighty commissions—the Pacify-the-West, Pacify-the-North, and Pacify-the-Barbarians generals—received silver seals with tiger knobs, three inches three fen square and nine fen thick, in willow-leaf seal script.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，嘗用上公佩將軍印，後以公、侯、伯及都督充總兵官，名曰：「掛印將軍」。

translations.literal: In the Hongwu reign, senior nobles once wore generals' seals; later dukes, marquises, earls, and regional commanders served as supreme commanders, styled "generals bearing the seal."
translations.idiomatic: During Hongwu, senior nobles once wore generals' seals; later dukes, marquises, earls, and regional commanders served as supreme commanders, styled "generals bearing the seal."

sentences.zh: 有事征伐，則命總兵佩印以往，旋師則上所佩印於朝。

translations.literal: When campaigns arose, the supreme commander was ordered to wear the seal on departure; on return the seal was presented at court.
translations.idiomatic: When campaigns arose, the supreme commander wore the seal on departure; on return he presented it at court.

sentences.zh: 此外，惟漕運總兵印同將軍。

translations.literal: Beyond this, only the seal of the grain-transport supreme commander matched that of a general.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond this, only the grain-transport supreme commander's seal matched that of a general.

sentences.zh: 其在外鎮守總兵、參將掛印，則洪熙元年始也。

translations.literal: The practice of regional garrison supreme commanders and deputy commanders bearing seals began only in Hongxi 1 (1425).
translations.idiomatic: Regional garrison supreme commanders and deputy commanders bearing seals began only in Hongxi 1 (1425).

sentences.zh: 有文臣掛將軍印者，王驥以兵部尚書徵湖、貴苗，掛平蠻將軍印；

translations.literal: There were civil officials who bore generals' seals: Wang Ji, as Minister of War campaigning against the Miao of Hunan and Guizhou, bore the Pacify-the-Barbarians general's seal;
translations.idiomatic: Civil officials sometimes bore generals' seals: Wang Ji, as Minister of War campaigning against the Miao of Hunan and Guizhou, bore the Pacify-the-Barbarians general's seal;

sentences.zh: 王越以左都御史守大同，掛徵西將軍印。

translations.literal: Wang Yue, as Left Censor-in-Chief defending Datong, bore the Pacify-the-West general's seal.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue, as Left Censor-in-Chief defending Datong, bore the Pacify-the-West general's seal.

sentences.zh: 其他文武大臣，有領敕而權重者，或給以銅關防，直紐，廣一寸九分五釐，長二寸九分，厚三分，九疊篆文，雖宰相行邊，與部曹無異。

translations.literal: Other civil and military grandees who held imperial commissions with heavy authority were sometimes given bronze pass seals, with straight knob, one inch nine fen five li wide, two inches nine fen long, three fen thick, and nine-fold seal script—even a chief minister on frontier duty was no different from a ministry bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Other civil and military grandees holding weighty imperial commissions were sometimes given bronze pass seals with straight knobs, one inch nine fen five li wide, two inches nine fen long, three fen thick, and nine-fold seal script—even a chief minister on frontier duty received the same as a ministry bureau.

sentences.zh: 惟正德時，張永徵安化王，用金鑄，嘉靖中，顧鼎臣居守，用牙鏤關防，皆特賜也。

translations.literal: Only in the Zhengde reign, when Zhang Yong campaigned against the Prince of Anhua, was gold used; in the Jiajing reign, when Gu Dingchen held the capital in the emperor's absence, an ivory-carved pass seal was used—both special grants.
translations.idiomatic: Only in the Zhengde reign, when Zhang Yong campaigned against the Prince of Anhua, was a gold pass seal granted; in Jiajing, when Gu Dingchen held the capital during the emperor's absence, an ivory-carved pass seal was granted—both were special bestowals.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖重御史之職，分河南等十三道，每道鑄二印，文曰：「繩愆糾繆」，守院御史掌其一，其一藏內府，有事則受以出，復命則納之。

translations.literal: At first the Taizu Emperor valued the censorate, dividing it into thirteen circuits such as Henan; each circuit cast two seals inscribed "Correct Faults and Rectify Errors"—the resident censor held one, one was stored in the inner palace; when business arose it was received for use, and on reporting back it was returned.
translations.idiomatic: Initially the Taizu Emperor valued the censorate, dividing it into thirteen circuits including Henan; each circuit cast two seals inscribed "Correct Faults and Rectify Errors"—the resident censor held one, the other was stored in the inner palace; when business arose it was issued, and on reporting back it was returned.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十三年，都御史袁泰言各道印篆相類。

translations.literal: In Hongwu 23 (1390), the Censor-in-Chief Yuan Tai said the seal scripts of the various circuits were too similar.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 23 (1390), Censor-in-Chief Yuan Tai reported that the seal scripts of the various circuits were too similar.

sentences.zh: 乃命改制某道監察御史，其奉差者，則曰：「巡按某處監察御史」，銅印直紐，有眼，方一寸五分，厚三分，八疊篆文。

translations.literal: The court then ordered them recast as "Censor of Such-and-Such Circuit"; those on commission read "Touring Censor of Such-and-Such Place," bronze seal with straight knob and perforation, one inch five fen square, three fen thick, eight-fold seal script.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered them recast as "Censor of [circuit name]"; those on commission read "Touring Censor of [place]," bronze seals with straight knobs and perforations, one inch five fen square, three fen thick, in eight-fold seal script.

sentences.zh: 成祖初幸北京，有一官署二三印者，夏原吉至兼掌九卿印，諸曹並於朝房取裁，其任重矣。

translations.literal: When the Chengzu Emperor first visited Beijing, one official might hold two or three seals; Xia Yuanji even concurrently held the seals of all nine chief ministers, and all bureaus took decisions in the morning chambers—the burden of office was heavy indeed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chengzu Emperor first visited Beijing, one official might hold two or three seals; Xia Yuanji even concurrently held the seals of all nine chief ministers, and all bureaus took decisions in the morning chambers—the burden of office was heavy indeed.

sentences.zh: 明初，賜高麗金印，龜紐，方三寸，文曰：「高麗國王之印」，賜安南鍍金銀印，駝紐，方三寸，文曰：「安南國王之印」。

translations.literal: In early Ming, Koryo was granted a gold seal with tortoise knob, three inches square, inscribed "Seal of the King of Koryo"; Annam was granted a gilt-silver seal with camel knob, three inches square, inscribed "Seal of the King of Annam."
translations.idiomatic: In early Ming, Koryo received a gold seal with tortoise knob, three inches square, inscribed "Seal of the King of Koryo"; Annam received a gilt-silver seal with camel knob, three inches square, inscribed "Seal of the King of Annam."

sentences.zh: 賜占城鍍金銀印，駝紐，方三寸，文曰：「占城國王之印」。

translations.literal: Champa was granted a gilt-silver seal with camel knob, three inches square, inscribed "Seal of the King of Champa."
translations.idiomatic: Champa received a gilt-silver seal with camel knob, three inches square, inscribed "Seal of the King of Champa."

sentences.zh: 賜吐蕃金印，駝紐，方五寸，文曰：「白蘭王印」。

translations.literal: Tibet was granted a gold seal with camel knob, five inches square, inscribed "Seal of the King of Bailan."
translations.idiomatic: Tibet received a gold seal with camel knob, five inches square, inscribed "Seal of the King of Bailan."

sentences.zh: 符牌：凡宣召親王，必遣官齎金符以往。

translations.literal: Tally plaques: Whenever a prince of the blood was summoned, an official was always dispatched bearing a gold tally.
translations.idiomatic: Tally plaques: Whenever a prince of the blood was summoned, an official was dispatched bearing a gold tally.

sentences.zh: 親王之籓及鎮守、巡撫諸官奏請符驗，俱從兵部奏，行尚寶司領之。

translations.literal: When princes went to their fiefs and garrison, grand coordinator, and other officials memorialized requesting tally verification, all proceeded through memorials to the Ministry of War and were issued by the Imperial Seals Office.
translations.idiomatic: When princes departed for their fiefs and garrison commanders, grand coordinators, and other officials requested tally verification, all proceeded through the Ministry of War and were issued by the Imperial Seals Office.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十六年定制：凡公差，以軍情重務及奉旨差遣給驛者，兵部既給勘合，即赴內府，關領符驗，給驛而去，事竣則繳。

translations.literal: Fixed in Hongwu 26 (1393): for all official missions involving weighty military affairs or imperial commission with relay service, once the Ministry of War had issued the travel warrant, one proceeded to the inner palace to obtain tally verification, received relay service and departed, and on completion returned it.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations fixed in Hongwu 26 (1393): for official missions involving weighty military affairs or imperial commission with relay service, once the Ministry of War issued the travel warrant, the envoy obtained tally verification at the inner palace, received relay service and departed, and returned the tally when the mission ended.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十七年定制：南京、鳳陽守備內外官，並各處鎮守總兵、巡撫，及各守一方不受鎮守節制內外守備，並領符驗奏事。

translations.literal: Fixed in Jiajing 37 (1558): garrison officials inside and outside Nanjing and Fengyang, all regional supreme commanders and grand coordinators, and all garrison commanders who held a region independently of supreme-commander control, all received tally verification for memorializing.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations fixed in Jiajing 37 (1558): garrison officials at Nanjing and Fengyang, all regional supreme commanders and grand coordinators, and garrison commanders holding independent jurisdictions all received tally verification for memorializing.

sentences.zh: 凡監槍、整飭兵備，並一城一堡守備官，不許關領符驗。

translations.literal: Officials supervising firearms, rectifying military preparedness, and garrison commanders of a single city or fort were not permitted to obtain tally verification.
translations.idiomatic: Officials supervising firearms, rectifying military preparedness, and garrison commanders of a single city or fort were not permitted to obtain tally verification.

sentences.zh: 其制，上織船馬之狀，起馬者用馬字型大小，起船者水字型大小，起雙馬者達字型大小，起單馬者通字型大小，起站船者信字型大小。

translations.literal: In form, the upper part wove the pattern of boat or horse: those requiring horses used the horse character size, those requiring boats the water character size, those requiring paired horses the da character size, those requiring single horses the tong character size, those requiring station boats the xin character size.
translations.idiomatic: In form, the upper part depicted boat or horse service: horse relays used the horse character size, boat relays the water character size, paired-horse relays the da character size, single-horse relays the tong character size, and station-boat relays the xin character size.

sentences.zh: 洪武四年，始制用寶金牌。

translations.literal: In Hongwu 4 (1371), imperial gold tally plaques were first instituted.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu 4 (1371), imperial gold tally plaques were first instituted.

sentences.zh: 凡軍機文書，自都督府、中書省長官而外，不許擅奏。

translations.literal: All military documents, apart from the chiefs of the Regional Military Commission and the Secretariat, might not be memorialized without authorization.
translations.idiomatic: All military documents, apart from the chiefs of the Regional Military Commission and the Secretariat, could not be memorialized without authorization.

sentences.zh: 有詔調軍，中書省同都督府覆奏，乃各出所藏金牌，入請用寶。

translations.literal: When an edict ordered troop movements, the Secretariat and Regional Military Commission jointly reported back; only then did each produce its stored gold tally and enter to request use of the imperial seal.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict ordered troop movements, the Secretariat and Regional Military Commission jointly reported back; only then did each produce its stored gold tally and request use of the imperial seal.

sentences.zh: 又造軍中調發符牌，用鐵，長五寸，闊半之，上鈒二飛龍，下鈒二麒麟，首為圜竅，貫以紅絲絛。

translations.literal: Army dispatch tally plaques were also made of iron, five inches long and half that wide; the upper part bore two flying dragons, the lower two qilin; the head had a round perforation threaded with red silk cord.
translations.idiomatic: Army dispatch tally plaques were also made of iron, five inches long and half that wide; the upper part bore two flying dragons, the lower two qilin; the head had a round perforation threaded with red silk cord.

sentences.zh: 嘗遣官齎金牌、信符詣西番，以茶易馬。

translations.literal: Officials were once dispatched bearing gold tallies and credential plaques to the Western Regions to trade tea for horses.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were once dispatched bearing gold tallies and credential plaques to the Western Regions to trade tea for horses.

sentences.zh: 其牌四十一，上號藏內府，下號降各番，篆文曰：「皇帝聖旨」，左曰：「合當差發」，右曰：「不信者斬」。

translations.literal: There were forty-one such plaques: the upper numbers were stored in the inner palace, the lower numbers issued to the various tribes; the seal script read "Imperial Edict of the Emperor," at left "Due for Dispatch," at right "He Who Does Not Believe—Beheaded."
translations.idiomatic: There were forty-one such plaques: upper numbers were stored in the inner palace, lower numbers issued to the various tribes; the seal script read "Imperial Edict of the Emperor," at left "Due for Dispatch," at right "He Who Does Not Believe—Beheaded."

sentences.zh: 二十二年又頒西番金牌、信符。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year (1389) Western Regions gold tallies and credential plaques were again issued.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year (1389) Western Regions gold tallies and credential plaques were issued again.

sentences.zh: 其後番官款塞，皆齎原降牌符而至。

translations.literal: Thereafter when tribal officials came in submission to the frontier, they all brought the originally issued plaques and tallies.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter when tribal officials came in submission to the frontier, they all brought the originally issued plaques and tallies.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年制信符、金字紅牌給雲南諸蠻。

translations.literal: In Yongle 2 (1404) credential plaques and red plaques with gold characters were made and given to the various tribes of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 2 (1404) credential plaques and red plaques with gold characters were made and granted to the various tribes of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 凡歷代改元，則所頒外國信符、金牌，必更鑄新年號給之。

translations.literal: Whenever a dynasty changed its reign title, the credential plaques and gold tallies issued to foreign states were always recast with the new reign title and granted anew.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the dynasty changed its reign title, credential plaques and gold tallies issued to foreign states were recast with the new reign title and granted anew.

sentences.zh: 此符信之達於四裔者也。

translations.literal: These were the tally credentials that reached the four peripheries.
translations.idiomatic: These were the tally credentials extended to the four peripheries.

sentences.zh: 其武臣懸帶金牌，則洪武四年所造。

translations.literal: The gold tally plaques worn suspended by military officials were those made in Hongwu 4.
translations.idiomatic: The gold tally plaques worn suspended by military officials were those made in Hongwu 4.

sentences.zh: 闊二寸，長一尺，上鈒雙龍，下鈒二伏虎，牌首尾為圓竅，貫以紅絲絛。

translations.literal: They were two inches wide and one foot long; the upper part bore twin dragons, the lower two crouching tigers; head and tail had round perforations threaded with red silk cord.
translations.idiomatic: They were two inches wide and one foot long; the upper part bore twin dragons, the lower two crouching tigers; head and tail had round perforations threaded with red silk cord.

sentences.zh: 指揮佩金牌，雙雲龍，雙虎符。

translations.literal: Commanders wore gold plaques with paired cloud-dragons and paired tiger tallies.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders wore gold plaques with paired cloud-dragons and paired tiger tallies.

sentences.zh: 千戶佩鍍金銀牌，獨雲龍，獨虎符。

translations.literal: Battalion commanders wore gilt-silver plaques with single cloud-dragon and single tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: Battalion commanders wore gilt-silver plaques with a single cloud-dragon and single tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 百戶素雲銀牌符。

translations.literal: Company commanders wore plain-cloud silver plaque tallies.
translations.idiomatic: Company commanders wore plain-cloud silver plaque tallies.

sentences.zh: 太祖親為文鈒之曰：「上天祐民，朕乃率撫。

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor personally composed the inscription, which read, "Heaven protects the people; I lead and comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu Emperor personally composed the inscription: "Heaven protects the people; I lead and comfort them.

sentences.zh: 威加華夏，實憑虎臣。

translations.literal: Majesty extends over Huaxia, truly relying on tiger-like ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Majesty extends over Huaxia, truly relying on tiger-like warriors.

sentences.zh: 賜爾金符，永傳後嗣。

translations.literal: I bestow on you this gold tally, to be transmitted forever to your descendants."
translations.idiomatic: I bestow on you this gold tally, to be transmitted forever to your descendants."

sentences.zh: 」天子祀郊廟，若視學、耤田，勳衛扈從及公侯、駙馬、五府都督日直、錦衣衛當直，及都督率諸衛千百戶夜巡內皇城，金吾諸衛各輪官隨朝巡綽，俱給金牌，有龍者、虎者、麒麟者、獅者、雲者，以官為差。

translations.literal: " When the Son of Heaven sacrificed at the suburban altars and ancestral temples, or inspected the schools or plowed the sacred field, meritorious guards in attendance, dukes, marquises, earls, imperial sons-in-law, the five offices' regional commanders on daily duty, the Embroidered-Uniform Guard on duty, and regional commanders leading the guards' battalion and company commanders on night patrol of the inner imperial city, and the Brocade-Clad Guard and other guards each rotating officers to patrol with the court—all were given gold plaques, with dragon, tiger, qilin, lion, or cloud designs according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: " When the Son of Heaven sacrificed at suburban altars and ancestral temples, inspected schools, or plowed the sacred field, meritorious guards in attendance, nobles, imperial sons-in-law, regional commanders on daily duty, the Embroidered-Uniform Guard on duty, regional commanders leading night patrols of the inner imperial city, and the Brocade-Clad Guard and other guards rotating court patrol officers—all received gold plaques with dragon, tiger, qilin, lion, or cloud designs according to rank.

sentences.zh: 其扈駕金字銀牌，則洪武六年所造。

translations.literal: The gold-character silver plaques for escorting the imperial carriage were those made in Hongwu 6 (1373).
translations.idiomatic: The gold-character silver plaques for escorting the imperial carriage were made in Hongwu 6 (1373).

sentences.zh: 尋改為守衛金牌，以銅為之，塗以金，高一尺，闊三寸，分字型大小凡五。

translations.literal: They were soon changed to guard gold plaques, made of copper gilded with gold, one foot high and three inches wide, divided into five character sizes.
translations.idiomatic: They were soon changed to guard gold plaques of copper gilded with gold, one foot high and three inches wide, divided into five character sizes.

sentences.zh: 仁字型大小，上鈒獨龍蟠雲花，公、侯、伯、都督佩之。

translations.literal: The ren character size bore a solitary dragon coiled amid cloud flowers; dukes, marquises, earls, and regional commanders wore it.
translations.idiomatic: The ren character size bore a solitary dragon amid cloud flowers; dukes, marquises, earls, and regional commanders wore it.

sentences.zh: 義字型大小，鈒伏虎盤雲花，指揮佩之。

translations.literal: The yi character size bore a crouching tiger amid coiled cloud flowers; commanders wore it.
translations.idiomatic: The yi character size bore a crouching tiger amid cloud flowers; commanders wore it.

sentences.zh: 禮字型大小，獬貂豸蟠雲花，千戶、衛鎮撫佩之。

translations.literal: The li character size bore a xiezhi beast amid coiled cloud flowers; battalion commanders and guard commissioners wore it.
translations.idiomatic: The li character size bore a xiezhi beast amid cloud flowers; battalion commanders and guard commissioners wore it.

sentences.zh: 智字型大小，鈒獅子蟠雲花，百戶、所鎮撫佩之。

translations.literal: The zhi character size bore a lion amid coiled cloud flowers; company commanders and company commissioners wore it.
translations.idiomatic: The zhi character size bore a lion amid cloud flowers; company commanders and company commissioners wore it.

sentences.zh: 信字型大小，鈒蟠雲花，將軍佩之。

translations.literal: The xin character size bore coiled cloud flowers; generals wore it.
translations.idiomatic: The xin character size bore coiled cloud flowers; generals wore it.

sentences.zh: 牌下鑄「守衛。

translations.literal: Below the plaque were cast the two seal characters "Guard."
translations.idiomatic: Below the plaque were cast the two seal characters "Guard."

sentences.zh: 」二篆字，背鑄「凡守衛官軍懸帶此牌。

translations.literal: " On the reverse were cast twenty-four characters: "All guard officers and soldiers who suspend this plaque."
translations.idiomatic: " On the reverse were cast twenty-four characters: "All guard officers and soldiers who suspend this plaque."

sentences.zh: 」等二十四字，牌首竅貫青絲。

translations.literal: " and so forth; the head of the plaque had a perforation threaded with blue silk.
translations.idiomatic: " The head of the plaque had a perforation threaded with blue silk.

sentences.zh: 鎮撫及將軍隨駕直宿衛者佩之，下直則納之。

translations.literal: Guard commissioners and generals on direct imperial escort duty wore them; when off duty they returned them.
translations.idiomatic: Guard commissioners and generals on direct imperial escort duty wore them; when off duty they returned them.

sentences.zh: 凡夜巡官，於尚寶司領權杖，禁城各門、金吾等衛指揮、千戶，分領申字型大小牌，午門自一至四，長安左右門、東華門自五至八，西華門自九至十二，玄武門自十三至十六。

translations.literal: All night-patrol officers obtained authority staffs from the Imperial Seals Office; commanders and battalion commanders of the Brocade-Clad Guard and other guards at the Forbidden City's gates each took charge of shen character size plaques—Meridian Gate numbers one through four, the left and right Chang'an gates and East Flowery Gate five through eight, West Flowery Gate nine through twelve, North Mystical Gate thirteen through sixteen.
translations.idiomatic: Night-patrol officers obtained authority staffs from the Imperial Seals Office; commanders and battalion commanders at the Forbidden City's gates each took charge of shen character size plaques—Meridian Gate numbers one through four, the Chang'an gates and East Flowery Gate five through eight, West Flowery Gate nine through twelve, North Mystical Gate thirteen through sixteen.

sentences.zh: 五城兵馬指揮亦日領權杖，東西南北中城，分領木、金、火、水、土五字型大小。

translations.literal: The Five-City Cavalry Command also daily received authority staffs; east, south, west, north, and central cities each took charge of wood, metal, fire, water, and earth character sizes.
translations.idiomatic: The Five-City Cavalry Command also received daily authority staffs; the east, south, west, north, and central districts each took charge of wood, metal, fire, water, and earth character sizes.

sentences.zh: 留守五衛、巡城官並金吾等衛守衛官，俱領銅符。

translations.literal: The five capital-garrison guards, city-patrol officers, and guard officers of the Brocade-Clad Guard and other guards all received bronze tallies.
translations.idiomatic: The five capital-garrison guards, city-patrol officers, and guard officers of the Brocade-Clad Guard and other guards all received bronze tallies.

sentences.zh: 留守衛指揮所領承字及東西北字型大小牌，俱左半字陽文，左比。

translations.literal: Commanders of the capital-garrison guards who received cheng character and east-west-north character size plaques all had the left half in raised characters, matched on the left.
translations.idiomatic: Capital-garrison commanders who received cheng character and east-west-north character size plaques all had the left half in raised characters, matched on the left.

sentences.zh: 金吾等衛，端門、承天門、東西北安門指揮千戶所領承字及東西北字型大小，俱右半字陰文，右比。

translations.literal: The Brocade-Clad Guard and others, and commanders and battalion commanders at the Upright Gate, Gate of Receiving Heaven, and the east, west, north, and Peace gates who received cheng character and east-west-north character sizes, all had the right half in intaglio, matched on the right.
translations.idiomatic: The Brocade-Clad Guard and commanders and battalion commanders at the Upright Gate, Gate of Receiving Heaven, and the east, west, north, and Peace gates who received cheng character and east-west-north character sizes all had the right half in intaglio, matched on the right.

sentences.zh: 銅符字型大小比對相同，方許巡行。

translations.literal: Only when the bronze tally character sizes matched on comparison was patrol permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Patrol was permitted only when the bronze tally character sizes matched.

sentences.zh: 內官、內使之出，亦須守門官比對銅符而後行。

translations.literal: When palace eunuchs and inner attendants went out, gate officers also had to compare bronze tallies before they might pass.
translations.idiomatic: When palace eunuchs and inner attendants went out, gate officers had to compare bronze tallies before allowing passage.

sentences.zh: 皇城九門守衛軍與圍子手，各領勇字型大小銅牌。

translations.literal: The guard soldiers and encircling archers at the imperial city's nine gates each received yong character size bronze plaques.
translations.idiomatic: Guard soldiers and encircling archers at the imperial city's nine gates each received yong character size bronze plaques.

sentences.zh: 錦衣校尉上直及光祿寺吏典廚役，遇大祀，俱佩雙魚銅牌。

translations.literal: Embroidered-Uniform Guard corporals on duty and clerks and kitchen servants of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, on great sacrifices, all wore paired-fish bronze plaques.
translations.idiomatic: Embroidered-Uniform Guard corporals on duty and clerks and kitchen servants of the Court of Imperial Entertainments all wore paired-fish bronze plaques during great sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 永樂六年駕幸北京，扈從官俱帶牙牌；

translations.literal: In Yongle 6 (1408), when the emperor visited Beijing, all escorting officials wore ivory plaques;
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 6 (1408), when the emperor visited Beijing, all escorting officials wore ivory plaques;

sentences.zh: 五府、六部、都察院、大理寺、錦衣衛各鑄印信，通政司、鴻臚寺各鑄關防，謂之行在衛門印信關防。

translations.literal: the five offices, Six Ministries, Censorate, Court of Judicial Review, and Embroidered-Uniform Guard each cast seals, the Office of Transmission and Court of State Ceremonial each cast pass seals—called the traveling-capital guard-gate seals and pass seals.
translations.idiomatic: the five offices, Six Ministries, Censorate, Court of Judicial Review, and Embroidered-Uniform Guard each cast seals, the Office of Transmission and Court of State Ceremonial each cast pass seals—called the traveling-capital guard-gate seals and pass seals.

sentences.zh: 其後命內府印綬監收貯。

translations.literal: Later they were ordered stored by the inner palace's Seal and Ribbon Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Later they were ordered stored by the inner palace's Seal and Ribbon Directorate.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十八年南巡，禮部領出，以給扈從者焉。

translations.literal: On the southern tour of Jiajing 18 (1539), the Ministry of Rites issued them to give to those in the imperial entourage.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern tour of Jiajing 18 (1539), the Ministry of Rites issued them to the imperial entourage.

sentences.zh: 凡郊廟諸祭陪祀供事官及執事者，入壇俱領牙牌，洪武八年始也。

translations.literal: All accompanying-sacrifice and service officials and ritual attendants at suburban altar sacrifices, on entering the altar precinct, all received ivory plaques—beginning in Hongwu 8 (1375).
translations.idiomatic: All accompanying-sacrifice officials, service officials, and ritual attendants at suburban altar sacrifices received ivory plaques on entering the altar precinct—beginning in Hongwu 8 (1375).

sentences.zh: 圓花牌，陪祀官領之。

translations.literal: Round floral plaques were received by accompanying-sacrifice officials.
translations.idiomatic: Accompanying-sacrifice officials received round floral plaques.

sentences.zh: 長花牌，供事官領之。

translations.literal: Long floral plaques were received by service officials.
translations.idiomatic: Service officials received long floral plaques.

sentences.zh: 長素牌，執事人領之。

translations.literal: Long plain plaques were received by ritual attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual attendants received long plain plaques.

sentences.zh: 又謂之祀牌。

translations.literal: They were also called sacrifice plaques.
translations.idiomatic: They were also called sacrifice plaques.

sentences.zh: 凡駕詣陵寢，扈從官俱於尚寶司領小牙牌。

translations.literal: Whenever the imperial carriage went to the mausoleums, all officials in the entourage received small ivory plaques from the Imperial Seals Office.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the imperial carriage went to the mausoleums, all officials in the entourage received small ivory plaques from the Imperial Seals Office.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖九年，皇后行親蠶禮，文官四品以上、武官三品以上命婦及使人，俱於尚寶司領牙牌，有雲花圜牌、鳥形長牌之異。

translations.literal: In Jiajing 9 (1530), when the empress performed the personal silkworm-raising rite, civil officials of rank 4a and above, military officials' wives of rank 3a and above, and envoys all received ivory plaques from the Imperial Seals Office, with round cloud-flower plaques and long bird-shaped plaques differing.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 9 (1530), when the empress performed the personal silkworm-raising rite, civil officials of rank 4a and above, military officials' wives of rank 3a and above, and envoys all received ivory plaques from the Imperial Seals Office—round cloud-flower plaques and long bird-shaped plaques among them.

sentences.zh: 凡文武朝參官、錦衣衛當駕官，亦領牙牌，以防奸偽，洪武十一年始也。

translations.literal: All civil and military officials attending court audience and Embroidered-Uniform Guard officers on imperial escort duty also received ivory plaques to guard against imposture—beginning in Hongwu 11 (1378).
translations.idiomatic: All civil and military officials attending court audience and Embroidered-Uniform Guard officers on imperial escort duty also received ivory plaques to guard against imposture—beginning in Hongwu 11 (1378).

sentences.zh: 其制，以象牙為之，刻官職於上。

translations.literal: In form they were of ivory, with office inscribed upon them.
translations.idiomatic: They were made of ivory, with the bearer's office inscribed upon them.

sentences.zh: 不佩則門者卻之，私相借者論如律。

translations.literal: Without wearing one, gatekeepers turned one away; private lending was prosecuted according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Without wearing one, gatekeepers turned the bearer away; private lending was prosecuted according to law.

sentences.zh: 牙牌字型大小，公、侯、伯以勳字，駙馬都尉以親字，文官以文字，武官以武字，教坊官以樂字，入內官以官字。

translations.literal: Ivory plaque character sizes: dukes, marquises, and earls used the merit character; imperial sons-in-law the kin character; civil officials the civil character; military officials the military character; music-bureau officials the music character; inner-palace officials the office character.
translations.idiomatic: Ivory plaque character sizes: dukes, marquises, and earls used the merit character; imperial sons-in-law the kin character; civil officials the civil character; military officials the military character; music-bureau officials the music character; inner-palace officials the office character.

sentences.zh: 正德十六年，禮科邢寰言：「牙牌惟常朝職官得懸。

translations.literal: In Zhengde 16 (1521), Xing Huan of the Ministry of Rites Section said, "Ivory plaques may be worn suspended only by officials in regular court attendance.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 16 (1521), Xing Huan of the Ministry of Rites Section said, "Ivory plaques may be worn only by officials in regular court attendance.

sentences.zh: 比來權奸侵柄，傳旨升官者輒佩牙牌，宜清核以重名器。

translations.literal: Recently powerful traitors have encroached on authority; those promoted by transmitted edict have promptly worn ivory plaques. A clearing audit is needed to restore weight to titles and insignia."
translations.idiomatic: Recently powerful traitors have encroached on authority; those promoted by transmitted edict have promptly worn ivory plaques. A clearing audit is needed to restore weight to titles and insignia."

sentences.zh: 」乃命文職不朝參者，毋得濫給牙牌；

translations.literal: " The court then ordered that civil officials not attending court audience must not be given ivory plaques indiscriminately;
translations.idiomatic: " The court then ordered that civil officials not attending court audience must not be given ivory plaques indiscriminately;

sentences.zh: 武官進禦侍班、佩刀、執金爐者給與。

translations.literal: military officials who entered the imperial presence to attend, wore swords, or carried the golden censer were to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: military officials who entered the imperial presence to attend, wore swords, or carried the golden censer were to receive them.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十八年，內府供事匠作、武職官皆帶朝參牙牌，嘗奉旨革奪，旋復給之。

translations.literal: In Jiajing 28 (1549), inner-palace service craftsmen and military officials all wore court-audience ivory plaques; an imperial order once stripped them, but they were soon issued again.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 28 (1549), inner-palace service craftsmen and military officials all wore court-audience ivory plaques; an imperial order once stripped them, but they were soon issued again.

sentences.zh: 給事中陳邦修以為言，禮部覆奏：「《會典》所載，文武官出入禁門帶牙牌，有執事、供事、朝參之別。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Chen Bangxiu spoke on the matter; the Ministry of Rites reported back: "The Collected Statutes record that civil and military officials entering and leaving the forbidden gates wear ivory plaques, with distinctions for ritual attendance, service, and court audience.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Chen Bangxiu spoke on the matter; the Ministry of Rites reported back: "The Collected Statutes record that civil and military officials entering and leaving the forbidden gates wear ivory plaques, with distinctions for ritual attendance, service, and court audience.

sentences.zh: 執事、供事者，皆屆期而領，如期而繳。

translations.literal: Those on ritual or service duty all received them when the term arrived and returned them when due.
translations.idiomatic: Those on ritual or service duty received them when the term arrived and returned them when due.

sentences.zh: 惟朝參牙牌，得朝夕懸之，非徒為關防之具，亦以示等威之辨也。

translations.literal: Only court-audience ivory plaques might be worn morning and evening; they were not merely passes for control, but also showed distinctions of rank and dignity.
translations.idiomatic: Only court-audience ivory plaques might be worn morning and evening; they were not merely passes for control, but also marked distinctions of rank and dignity.

sentences.zh: 虛銜帶俸、供事、執事者，不宜概領。

translations.literal: Those with empty titles drawing stipends, and those on service or ritual duty, should not all receive them indiscriminately.
translations.idiomatic: Those with empty titles drawing stipends, and those on service or ritual duty, should not all receive them indiscriminately.

sentences.zh: 第出入禁闥，若一切革奪，何由譏察？

translations.literal: Yet for entering and leaving the forbidden inner gates, if all were stripped away entirely, how could wrongdoing be detected?
translations.idiomatic: Yet for entering and leaving the forbidden inner gates, if all plaques were stripped away entirely, how could misconduct be detected?

sentences.zh: 尚寶司所貯舊牌數百，上有『入內府』字型大小，請以給之。

translations.literal: The Imperial Seals Office stores several hundred old plaques bearing the "Enter Inner Palace" character size; please issue these.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Seals Office stores several hundred old plaques bearing the "Enter Inner Palace" character size; please issue these.

sentences.zh: 至於衛所武官，掌印、僉書侍衛之外，非屬朝參供役者，盡革奪之。

translations.literal: As for guard-unit military officials, apart from seal-holders, registrars, and attendants on guard duty, all not belonging to court audience or service should have them entirely stripped.
translations.idiomatic: As for guard-unit military officials, apart from seal-holders, registrars, and attendants on guard duty, all not belonging to court audience or service should have them entirely stripped.

sentences.zh: 其納粟、填注冒賜牙牌及罷退閑住官舊所關領不繳者，俱逮問。

translations.literal: Those who bought grain for office, filled in registers to obtain plaques by fraud, and dismissed or idle officials who had received them but not returned them—all were to be arrested and questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Those who bought office with grain, obtained plaques by fraud, and dismissed or idle officials who had not returned old plaques—all were to be arrested and questioned.

sentences.zh: 」報可。

translations.literal: " Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 洪武十五年，制使節，黃色三簷寶蓋，長二尺，黃紗袋籠之。

translations.literal: In Hongwu 15 (1382), credentials of office were made: a yellow triple-eaved precious canopy two feet long, enclosed in a yellow gauze bag.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Hongwu, credentials of office were instituted: a yellow triple-eaved precious canopy two feet long, kept in a yellow gauze bag.

sentences.zh: 又制丹漆架一，以節置其上。

translations.literal: A vermilion-lacquered stand was also made, on which the staff was placed.
translations.idiomatic: A vermilion-lacquered stand was also made to hold the staff.

sentences.zh: 使者受命，則載以行；

translations.literal: When an envoy received his commission, he carried it on his journey;
translations.idiomatic: When an envoy received his commission, he carried the staff on his journey;

sentences.zh: 使歸，則持之以復命。

translations.literal: when the envoy returned, he bore it back to report completion of the mission.
translations.idiomatic: when he returned, he bore it back to report on his mission.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，詔考定使節之制，禮部奏：「漢光武時，以竹為節，柄長八尺，其毛三重。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, an edict ordered study and fixing of the staff of office; the Ministry of Rites reported: "In the time of Emperor Guangwu of Han, bamboo was used for the staff, the handle eight feet long, with three tiers of tufts.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, an edict ordered the regulations for credentials of office to be examined and fixed; the Ministry of Rites reported: "In the reign of Emperor Guangwu of Han, bamboo was used for the staff, with a handle eight feet long and three tiers of tufts.

sentences.zh: 而黃公紹《韻會》註：漢節柄長三尺，毛三重，以旄牛為之。

translations.literal: But Huang Gongshao's Collected Rhymes notes: Han staffs had handles three feet long, three tiers of tufts, made of yak tail.
translations.idiomatic: But Huang Gongshao's annotation in the Collected Rhymes states that Han staffs had handles three feet long, with three tiers of tufts made from yak tail.

sentences.zh: 」詔從三尺之制。

translations.literal: " The edict followed the three-foot regulation.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict adopted the three-foot standard.

sentences.zh: 宮室之制：吳元年作新內。

translations.literal: Regulations for palace buildings: In the first year of Wu, a new inner palace was built.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations for palace buildings: In the first year of Wu, a new inner palace was constructed.

sentences.zh: 正殿曰奉天殿，後曰華蓋殿，又後曰謹身殿，皆翼以廊廡。

translations.literal: The main hall was called Hall of Complying with Heaven; behind it Hall of the Imperial Canopy; still behind it Hall of Cultivating the Person—all flanked by covered corridors.
translations.idiomatic: The main hall was called the Hall of Complying with Heaven; behind it stood the Hall of the Imperial Canopy, and behind that the Hall of Cultivating the Person—all flanked by covered corridors.

sentences.zh: 奉天殿之前曰奉天門，殿左曰文樓，右曰武樓。

translations.literal: Before the Hall of Complying with Heaven was the Gate of Complying with Heaven; to the hall's left was Literary Tower, to the right Martial Tower.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Hall of Complying with Heaven stood the Gate of Complying with Heaven; to the left of the hall was the Literary Tower, to the right the Martial Tower.

sentences.zh: 謹身殿之後為宮，前曰乾清，後曰坤甯，六宮以次列。

translations.literal: Behind the Hall of Cultivating the Person lay the palace quarters: in front, Palace of Celestial Purity; behind, Palace of Earthly Tranquility; the six palaces ranged in order.
translations.idiomatic: Behind the Hall of Cultivating the Person lay the residential palaces: in front, the Palace of Celestial Purity; behind, the Palace of Earthly Tranquility; the six palaces were arrayed in sequence.

sentences.zh: 宮殿之外，周以皇城，城之門，南曰午門，東曰東華，西曰西華，北曰玄武。

translations.literal: Outside the palace buildings, the Imperial City enclosed them; the city's gates: south, Meridian Gate; east, East Flowery Gate; west, West Flowery Gate; north, North Mystical Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the palace buildings, the Imperial City enclosed them. The city gates were: to the south, the Meridian Gate; to the east, the East Flowery Gate; to the west, the West Flowery Gate; to the north, the North Mystical Gate.
